searchText: <@552133098075193354> would you mind including EIP-6122 (Forkid checks based on timestamps) https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6122 in the https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/master/network-upgrades/mainnet-upgrades/shanghai.md#eips-considered-for-inclusion list? Also could we get a tracker for 6049? Would be good to have client versions with all 6 EIPs merged before we go for sepolia fork. So, we usually don't include non-core EIPs in the hard fork spec, but I'm not against doing it. Just curious what client teams think! Re: 6049, what do you think the tracker should track 🤔 ? Because it's just a deprecation warning, there isn't really anything for clients to do Don't they have to add the deprecation warning? 😄 I think it's up to them if/how they want to do it. IMO it's more valuable for infra providers to add this, as that's where it gets "seen", i.e. solidity, etherscan,etc. Generally I haven't seen clients provide warnings to smart-contract layer issues, as they are all expected to be indistinguishable at runtime. For 6049 I don't see anything for client to do except for maybe a line in release notes. Any value of "here, we warned you" belongs not in client release notes but in EIPs, IMHO. I also see EIP-6122 as not tied to a hard fork. The last similar one, Eth/66 (eip-2481) was not tied to a hard fork and shipped independently. A tracker would be useful but I don't think it's a go/no-go for a hard fork like, say, PUSH0 is. The negative impact is to the client and not to the whole network. The other 4 EIPs are all merged, per the spec tracker - https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/master/network-upgrades/mainnet-upgrades/shanghai.md#implementation-progresss Right, maybe we should have a Core EIP that says "we're now using a timestamp on the EL"? which isn't about the peering, but focused on "the fork's changes will trigger at timestamp X, not block Y (or TTD Z)" Yes, that is the real impact of 6122 is that timestamps are a one-way door for fork activation. In https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs we also have a section called `Some clarifications were enabled without protocol releases:`. Perhaps these fit there? Yeah, we can definitely add something there. Maybe we can also add it in the fork-view of the executable specs? That's one neat thing about the way the CL specs are rendered by default which we don't quite have.
